title: Where to Look Next: Frontiers, and the Difference Between Done and Stuck

questions.question: A rover is dropped into an unknown building. Where should it go first?
options: To where what is known meets what is not: a free cell with an unseen cell beside it

questions.question: Which of these is a frontier cell?
options: A wall next to an unknown cell
A free cell with an unknown cell directly beside it, up, down, left or right
Any cell at the edge of the map
questions.explanation: A wall is known and an unknown cell cannot be stood in.

questions.question: Why choose the nearest opening by the way the rover would drive?
options: The straight line can go through a wall: from (5,5) the nearest in a line was 34 steps to drive and the chosen one 24
It is more accurate to the metre
questions.explanation: The test checked the choice against its own search.

questions.question: What does a minimum size for an opening do?
options: Keeps the rover from driving across the room to look at a single missed cell: a minimum of 5 went to the real opening and a minimum of 1 to the speck
questions.explanation: A speck made a second opening of 4 cells.

questions.question: What are the three answers when choosing a frontier?
options: Found, finished (nothing left of that size) and unreachable (some left and no route over free cells)
questions.explanation: A rover shut in is not finished.

questions.question: What does a version with only 'no goal' lose?
options: The difference between a rover that has finished and one that is shut in, which look the same
questions.explanation: A sealed room with a sliver seen through a window gave unreachable.
